hook: Airline swapped direct Phuket flights for *11-hour* layover: pays ₹70,000
hook_b: Airline swapped direct Phuket flights for *11-hour* layover: pays ₹70,000
tldr: A Telangana consumer commission held an airline liable for deficiency in service after it cancelled a family's booked non-stop Hyderabad–Phuket flights and moved them to connecting flights.

beats.what: The family paid ₹1,16,477 for four round-trip tickets (June 6–13, 2026); on May 21 the airline cancelled them and rebooked via Bengaluru, with an 11-hour halt on return.
beats.why: The airline cited winter schedule changes and operational reasons but did not substantiate why confirmed flights were cancelled, the commission found.
beats.care: Passengers whose flights are cancelled or rescheduled can approach a consumer commission; airlines must assist passengers during long halts.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Award: ₹15,000 per passenger (₹60,000) plus ₹10,000 litigation costs. The family had paid for its own stay during the Bengaluru stopover.

cards.q: Has an airline ever changed your booked flight?

qs: What assistance are airlines required to give during long halts caused by rescheduling?
How long do such consumer cases usually take to be decided?

facts.t: The family also paid *₹2,949* extra for baggage, and had non-refundable Phuket hotel bookings.

viz.verdict: Passengers recover about 60% of the fare for the disruption.
Rescheduling without valid reason cost the airline.

learn.t: Deficiency in service = a legal term under consumer law for a shortfall in quality or manner of a service that was promised.

watch: Whether the airline appeals the order.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Telangana consumer commission orders airline to pay Rs 70,000

fact: Consumer commission orders an airline to pay a Hyderabad family *₹70,000*
twist: The airline's counsel appeared, but it never filed a written reply within *45 days*, so its right to respond was closed.
